clue.text: Escapes bicycle finally going into vehicle — what made cyclist go close?

parts.note: slips, as in slips away or gives someone the slip

indicators.note: the final letter of the bike is put inside the vehicle's letters

parts.note: a tram is a public vehicle running on rails

indicators.note: points to the last letter of the word bicycle

explanation.surface: A bike escapes into the path of a vehicle as a cyclist edges near.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyclist tucks into the low-pressure wake behind another rider or vehicle to save effort, drawing up close behind it.

clue.text: Very wet politician with external influence

indicators.note: the influence word sits outside, wrapping around the politician

parts.note: sway means power or influence over others

explanation.surface: An outsider swaying a politician who is feeble, or 'wet'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very wet' hints at a feeble politician (British 'wet' means weak), but here it means boggy.
explanation.definitionFit: Marshy ground is waterlogged and soggy, the sense of very wet land.

clue.text: Having arrived with idea half-formed, the German female revolutionised US corporation

indicators.note: turned right round, so the whole string of pieces is read backwards
only the first half of the word idea is used

parts.note: der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A German woman, arriving with a half-baked idea, overturns an American company.
explanation.definitionFit: The Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation is a large American mortgage company known by this nickname.

clue.text: Rye you dumped in extra farm building

indicators.note: what remains of the grain word goes inside the extra

parts.note: a bye is an extra run in cricket, scored without the batter hitting the ball

indicators.note: the letters for you are thrown out of the word rye

parts.note: ye is an old form of you

explanation.surface: Throwing away surplus rye into an outbuilding on the farm.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing YE from RYE leaves R. A bye is a run in cricket scored when the ball is missed by both batter and wicketkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowshed is a farm outbuilding where cattle are kept.

clue.text: Celebrity hugging party host, a name on the up in capital city

indicators.note: the celebrity word wraps around the party host

parts.note: a big name is a celebrity
a DJ hosts the music at a party

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters are read backwards

explanation.surface: A star embraces the person running the party, his name rising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Celebrity' and 'name' both mean a famous person on the surface, but the second gives only its abbreviation. In a down clue 'on the up' means read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the capital of Chad in central Africa.

clue.text: Time off work, day off for spring festival

indicators.note: day is taken off, removed from the leave word

parts.note: a holiday is time off work

explanation.surface: Taking a day off work for a festival in spring.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hindu festival of colours is celebrated in spring, around March.

clue.text: Two similar groups interlocking to form musical ensemble

indicators.note: the two copies overlap where they meet, so the middle letters trade places
the group word is written twice, side by side

explanation.surface: Two matching bands joining together to make one musical group.
explanation.walkthrough: SETSET with the central T and S swapped, so the two copies lock together, gives SE-ST-ET.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of six performers, also a six-line verse, is a musical ensemble of that size.

clue.text: Gee — wonderful army's beaten, suffering after conflict

parts.note: gee is the letter G spelt out

indicators.note: beaten like eggs, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: An exclamation as a fine army is defeated and suffers after the war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gee' looks like a cry of surprise, but it gives the letter G.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name for chronic illnesses reported by veterans of the 1991 Middle East war.

clue.text: Wild animal dung for manure Bill's imported

indicators.note: the bill is brought inside the dung word

parts.note: guano is bird or bat droppings used as fertiliser
AC, short for account, is a bill

explanation.surface: Bill brings in animal dung to use on the land.
explanation.definitionFit: A South American camelid related to the llama, living wild in the Andes.

clue.text: Physics unit within campus

indicators.note: the letters are found inside the word campus

explanation.surface: A unit of physics taught on a university site.
explanation.definitionFit: The ampere is the SI base unit of electric current.

clue.text: This writer long opposing high-ranking expert devoted to past era

parts.note: the setter referring to himself, me
to long for something is to be dying for it, so die

explanation.surface: The setter, against a top expert, longs for a bygone age.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar of the Middle Ages specialises in that historical period.

clue.text: Nervous and unpleasant couples (two of them) swapping round

indicators.note: within each of the first two pairs of letters the order is switched

explanation.surface: Anxious and unpleasant pairs, two of them, changing partners.
explanation.walkthrough: NA becomes AN and ST becomes TS, with Y left in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal American usage for jittery or fidgety, as if ants were crawling on you.

clue.text: Troubled home leads to nasty chatter

indicators.note: turning nasty, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Home life in trouble leads to spiteful gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: A British idiom for being in serious difficulty or in a mess.

clue.text: Assesses the speed of fast movers offering holiday accommodation?

explanation.surface: Clocking how quickly fast runners go, then offering a holiday place.
explanation.definitionFit: Part-ownership deals giving the right to use a holiday property for set weeks each year.

clue.text: Model taking a drug, explosive old girl

explanation.surface: A model takes drugs, like a wild former schoolgirl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old girl' looks like one phrase but splits into O and SIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The supreme or ideal example of something, its perfect embodiment.

clue.text: Bodily fold in stomach — an initial sign

indicators.note: the sign comes first, before the stomach word

parts.note: an omen is a sign or portent
tum is a childish word for stomach

explanation.surface: A first warning sign of trouble in the gut.
explanation.definitionFit: A fold of the peritoneum that hangs from the stomach in front of the intestines.

clue.text: Hat sailor laid on bunk, having eaten nothing

indicators.note: in a down clue the sailor sits above the rest

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

indicators.note: the bunk word takes in the zero

explanation.surface: A sailor lying on his bunk with an empty stomach, wearing his hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunk' suggests a bed, but it is nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: A fez-like brimless cap worn by Muslim men, usually red with a tassel.

clue.text: Fuss when there's evidence of cats around fields

indicators.note: the cat noises go round the fuss

parts.note: mews are the cries cats make

explanation.surface: A commotion when cat signs turn up around the fields.
explanation.definitionFit: Grassland areas, often mown for hay, are fields.

clue.text: Cleric and theology graduate, each featured in tabloid

indicators.note: the graduate and each appear inside the newspaper

parts.note: the Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

explanation.surface: A churchman and a divinity graduate both appearing in a tabloid paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral official ranking just below the dean.

clue.text: Trees in lanes enthralling a fellow no end

indicators.note: the lanes word holds the rest captive inside
the last letter is cut off the fellow word

explanation.surface: Woodland in country lanes, where a man becomes captivated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellow no end' means a man with his last letter cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: North American larches are conifers.

clue.text: Keys to get contents of medicine cupboards

definitions.meaning: in music the keynote of a scale gives a piece's key
restorative pick-me-up remedies kept with medicines

explanation.surface: Finding keys to open medicine cabinets.
explanation.definitionFit: The keynote of a scale names a key, and pick-me-up remedies stand in medicine cabinets.

clue.text: Housemate gives call to attract attention, having returned in taxi

indicators.note: the reversed call goes inside the taxi
the call is read backwards

parts.note: ho is a shout for attention

explanation.surface: A flatmate shouts for attention after getting back in a taxi.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for cohabitant, someone living together with another.

clue.text: One of two eating oysters in a fish restaurant?

definitions.meaning: in Lewis Carroll's poem The Walrus and the Carpenter, the pair eat the oysters
British slang for a fish-and-chip shop

explanation.surface: A diner tucking into oysters in a seafood restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: The oyster eaters are the Walrus and the Carpenter; 'chippy' is British slang for a carpenter. A chippy is also a British fish-and-chip shop, hence the query.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang names both a woodworker and a takeaway selling fried cod and fries.

clue.text: Clouds in Britain most unusual

indicators.note: the letters are made unusual, rearranged

explanation.surface: The cloud cover in Britain is most out of the ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey, rain-bearing layer clouds, the plural of nimbostratus.

clue.text: Star in the first half of amazing events

indicators.note: only the opening half of the word's letters is used

explanation.surface: A star features in the opening half of some wonders.
explanation.definitionFit: A variable red giant in the constellation Cetus, Omicron Ceti.

clue.text: Bird in tree noted for its leaves overlooking lake

indicators.note: in a down clue the tree sits above the lake

parts.note: the tea plant is grown for its leaves

explanation.surface: A bird perched in a leafy tree above a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A small dabbling duck, a waterbird.

clue.text: Cruel person wasting good money

indicators.note: the good is lost from the cruel person

parts.note: an ogre is a cruel brute

explanation.surface: A tyrant squandering good cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin and monetary unit of Denmark, Norway and Sweden.

clue.text: Member of religious sect coming out with 'Pish!' in cathedral

indicators.note: the letters come out differently, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone from a sect emerges with a scornful 'Pish!' inside a cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of a Christian sect founded in America in the nineteenth century, the Brethren in Christ.
